anchorShapeTaxonomy.why: Earned incrementally across all three children, at the cost of three review rounds plus an escalation-ladder attempt in S1. The choice of anchor shape is not stylistic - picking the wrong one produces a test that cannot fail against the very change it exists to catch.

shapes.pinned-literal: Value is offline-determinable. Pin the literal and compare. Discriminates any change to preimage OR serialization. The default.
shapes.independently-reconstructed-and-rehashed: Value embeds live per-run facts (frozen ref OIDs, worktree instance ids), so a fixed literal is PHYSICALLY impossible. The test rebuilds the hashed body from reported fields and rehashes with its OWN hardcoded hash calls, independent of production's encoding. Named by S2. CAUTION: this shape is blind to a SYMMETRIC change - if the test calls production's own serializer to rebuild, a serializer shift moves both sides together. S2 had to strengthen both such anchors with an offline-pinned literal over their non-Git-fact field slice.
shapes.behavioural: Value is NEVER externally observable - a purely internal key with no public type exposing it. Pinning its literal would pin an implementation detail. Anchor the OBSERVABLE property instead. Named by S3 for refs.ts:447's CommittedChangeEvidence.digest, an internal de-dup key: force two refs to a byte-identical Change -> listChanges reports exactly 1 entry; perturb only one copy in a field the schema never reads -> exactly 2 entries, one per foundAtRef. Proves the digest is a live discriminator in the dedup key rather than decoration.
shapes.relational: NOT A VALID ANCHOR. toMatch(shape), .toBe(other), .not.toBe(other), distinct-set counts. Uniformly blind to any change that transforms every value the same way - which is exactly what a preimage, digest or format change is. S1 passed 217/217 with every derived digest unanchored.

anchorShapeTaxonomy.selectionRule: Ask whether the value is externally observable, and whether a fixed literal is physically possible. Observable + determinable -> pinned literal. Observable + live facts -> reconstruct-and-rehash, PLUS an offline-pinned slice to cover the symmetric case. Not observable -> behavioural. Never relational.
anchorShapeTaxonomy.proofRule: For every anchor, the mutation used to prove it must discriminate THE PROPERTY THE ANCHOR EXISTS FOR, not merely make something go red. S2's near-miss: an input-field perturbation moves only one side of the comparison and is the break an un-strengthened anchor already catches; the symmetric serializer case went unmeasured until a verifier caught it.

leadBriefDefect.what: The LEAD's dispatch brief undercounted the capability set for ALL THREE children. It told each planner there were 2 capabilities; the real numbers were 3, 3 and 7 (S3 ported 6, correctly dropping store-planning-scope-routing which does not exist on this line).
leadBriefDefect.rootCause: The LEAD used the survey's `referenceSpecs` field as the inventory. That field is a SUMMARY, not a directory listing - it names the headline capabilities, not every spec file the prior-art change carries.
leadBriefDefect.fix: Always list the prior-art change's own specs/ directory (`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/dev/0.1.7 -- rasen/changes/archive/<change>/specs/`) rather than trusting any summarised count, including the LEAD's own.
leadBriefDefect.whyItMattered: Each planner caught it and proposed the true set anyway, so nothing shipped short. But a planner that trusted the brief would have under-delivered by a whole capability three times running, and the omission was invisible from inside the brief.
leadBriefDefect.generalForm: A summarised count carried forward as an inventory is the documentation-layer version of this portfolio's recurring defect: a claim that reads as complete because nothing in it can reveal what it left out.

toolingHazard.what: The bare `rasen` command on this machine is a GLOBALLY INSTALLED dev-local build at version 0.1.7 (dev.local 9472d7dc). This repo is 0.2.0. So `rasen ...` runs 0.1.7 code against 0.2.0 data.
toolingHazard.howItSurfaced: The S2 implementer hit `error: unknown option '--target-line'` running ported upstream tests. The LEAD had earlier run `rasen new change --help`, seen `--target-line <id>` in the output, and read it as a fact about this branch - it was a fact about the global 0.1.7 binary. `git grep target-line -- src/cli/index.ts src/commands/change.ts` on this branch returns NOTHING.
toolingHazard.rule: Use `node bin/rasen.js ...` for every rasen invocation in this worktree, never bare `rasen`.
toolingHazard.damageAssessment: The LEAD re-ran every load-bearing measurement against the local 0.2.0 build: `pipeline show auto-decompose --for-execution` (same 7 stages, same gate resolution to false via autopilot-global, same ship/archive sonnet stage models, same review-cycle maxRounds 3), `validate --strict` on both children (1 passed / 0 failed each), and `archive --dry-run` on child 1 (same tasks blocker). ALL IDENTICAL - no orchestration decision was corrupted. TASK_PATTERN is byte-identical between the two lines, so the [~] finding also stands.
toolingHazard.residualRisk: Worker-taken measurements that used the bare command may differ. Each worker has been told to re-take with the local build and report any that changed.

gateMethodologyFinding.what: The single full-suite gate run is no longer trustworthy on this machine at default parallelism. It came back RED - 3 files / 6 tests failed out of 122 files - and every one of the six passed on a solo re-run. No regression existed.

numbers.soloReRuns: store.test.ts + store-root-selection.test.ts -> 84 passed 0 failed; workspace-cleanup.test.ts -> 26 passed 0 failed

gateMethodologyFinding.cause: S2 adds suites an order of magnitude heavier than S1's pure unit tests - measured solo wall-clock: workspace-cleanup 166610ms, workspace-cli 166960ms, workspace-apply 109103ms - against a 30s testTimeout, pool 'forks', maxWorkers min(4, cpus), on Windows temp dirs with real Git worktrees.
gateMethodologyFinding.theTriageTrap: Two of the six failures were 30s timeouts and ONE was a hard assertion failure - `expected 1 to be +0`, a command exiting 1 instead of 0. That one also passed solo. So an assertion failure is NOT reliable evidence of a real defect on this machine: a busy filesystem makes commands genuinely fail, not merely run slow. The timeout-vs-assertion distinction does NOT separate contention from defect. Only a solo re-run does. Do not triage by failure shape.
gateMethodologyFinding.ruleForS3: S3 adds more heavy suites and will hit this harder. (1) Never triage a full-run failure by its shape - re-run the file solo before concluding anything. (2) Do not accept 'every file passes solo' AS the gate either; it is good evidence but a different claim from 'the suite passes'. Re-take the gate at reduced parallelism (VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2) for a trustworthy single number. (3) Only one agent runs suites at a time - the LEAD owns the gate, workers hold.
gateMethodologyFinding.alsoNote: KNOWN_SLOW_TEST_WEIGHTS_MS entries help CI SHARDING but do nothing for a single local full run. S2 added three; S3 must measure and add its own for any suite of comparable weight or the macOS/Windows shards will skew.

The gate reported 5 newly skipped tests, all in workspace-baseline.test.ts, but the implementer had reported SEVEN deferred cases - 5 there and 2 in store-v2-workspace-journey.test.ts. gateCoverageBlindSpot.generalRule: A gate command frozen at one point in time stops measuring whatever the subject grows afterwards, silently. Same disease as an assertion that cannot fail, one level up. Re-derive the gate's file list from the change's own diff each time rather than reusing a stale literal.

brandVocabularyGuardBlindSpot.severity: Trivial in S1, but with a LIVE consumer in both later children
brandVocabularyGuardBlindSpot.what: S1 ships a guard in test/core/store/planning-foundation-consumer.test.ts that reads branded-type declarations out of the Layer-0 sources and fails by name if a brand reaches the vocabulary without a bare-string pin. It closes the recurring 'a type assertion reached through a derived type is inert against its base' defect. But the guard reads exactly THREE hardcoded source files.
brandVocabularyGuardBlindSpot.consequence: S2 and S3 both add new modules to src/core/store/. Any brand declared in a file outside those three inherits NONE of this guard - the suite stays fully green. Two further blind spots, both requiring a deliberate act: a commented-out pin still counts as present (text scan), and a brand declared with a line break after the `=` is invisible while the count assertion still passes (there is no formatter backstop - no prettier config, lint is eslint only).
brandVocabularyGuardBlindSpot.actionForPlanner: When proposing S2 and S3, decide explicitly whether new branded types are in scope. If they are, extend the guard's source list in the same change that introduces them - do NOT leave a new brand unguarded and do not assume the S1 guard covers it.

relationalAssertionBlindness.what: S1's most expensive lesson, established over three review rounds plus an escalation-ladder attempt. A test suite built entirely from toMatch(shape), .toBe(other), .not.toBe(other) and distinct-set counts is UNIFORMLY BLIND to any change that transforms every value the same way - which is exactly what a preimage, digest, or serialization-format change does. Three consecutive rounds of 217/217 green missed it: the problem was never too few assertions, it was an assertion SHAPE structurally immune to the defect class.
relationalAssertionBlindness.actionForPlanner: S3 in particular ships executionPlanDigest and the Issue/Plan serializers - the same durable-format shape. Require known-input/known-digest golden vectors in the proposal, with pinned LITERAL inputs per vector (never chained off the previous derivation, or a break smears across all vectors instead of localising). Require that each vector also walks back through its own verifier, so a preimage change cannot hide behind a verifier that stopped checking.

portfolioLessons: The 0.1.7 TEST HELPERS are the real coupling graph, not the src imports. test/helpers/store-workspace-fixture.ts -> workspace/module.js and test/helpers/store-finalization-fixture.ts -> finalization/index.js are what actually decide slice boundaries here. Both scope surprises in this portfolio came from test/helpers/ and neither was visible in the src import graph. Any future 'can we port a subset of X' question in this codebase starts at test/helpers/, not at src/.

Keep ported file layout byte-comparable to origin/dev/0.1.7 wherever possible. That comparability is what makes the 9 archived 0.1.7 changes usable as a diff-able reference, and it is worth more than local tidiness. Concretely: do NOT extract the two string constants issues/ takes out of workspace/binding.ts (611 LOC) just because they look separable.
Re-run `git diff e62b101f origin/dev/0.2.0 -- src/core/store` before trusting any future claim that the store lines diverged. It is currently EMPTY and it is the cheapest possible check.
